- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to compensate for bearish sentiment bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overcorrects and underpredicts the next period; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to avoid overshoot lag.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending upward, model frequently overestimates near-term upside; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 periods to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment drops sharply (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.1) and price is falling, model often fails to recognize momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to counteract sentiment-induced downward bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates price in early periods (1–5 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish; apply +0.5–1.0% adjustment to first 5 forecast points.
